transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Reed (Redwood AE), Samira Ahmed (Redwood SE), Eli Torres (Redwood), Dr. Priya Kapoor, Michael Chen, Laura Perez, Aaron Holt, Nina Park (Veridian)
---
00:00:05 Jordan Reed: hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood. we also have Samira and Eli from the solutions team. how's everyone?
00:00:12 Dr. Priya Kapoor: good thanks. a quick note, we've got the clinical data folks on stand-by but they're not joining this call. main goals today are to map success criteria and the timeline for the POC.
00:00:25 Jordan Reed: perfect. high level, we want to scope the pilot so you can validate latency, throughput and quality with a representative workload, and then decide next steps - dedicated or hosted. does that sound right?
00:00:34 Michael Chen: yes. latency is the big one for us, sub-200ms 95p for short summaries; cost is second.
00:00:42 Samira Ahmed: got it, thanks Michael. can you share current traffic? QPS and average token length?
00:00:48 Aaron Holt: right now baseline is about 500 requests per minute during peak, average prompt length 120 tokens, response ~220 tokens, so ~340 tokens per request. daily active ~40k requests.
00:01:05 Eli Torres: that's helpful. for our benchmark plan we usually run hosted baseline, then a quantized private variant to compare cost/throughput. we'll also test prefix caching for common prompts.
00:01:20 Nina Park: for success criteria I'd propose: 1) latency 95p under 250ms for <512 token traces, 2) throughput to handle 1.2x peak, 3) cost per 1k tokens < target number (we gave an internal target), and 4) no data residency violations.
00:01:38 Jordan Reed: good list. Samira, can we translate that into benchmark pass plan?
00:01:43 Samira Ahmed: yes, propose three passes: baseline hosted with your sample traffic, tuned hosted (batching/kv cache), and quantized Dedicated/private variant. measure latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and per-token cost. allow 2-3 runs per pass for variance.
00:02:00 Laura Perez: security side - we require SOC2, SSO/SAML for access, audit logs, and KMS integration for key control. also need an NDA and data handling agreement for the anonymized dataset.
00:02:12 Jordan Reed: understood. we will send our SOC2 and ISO artifacts, and a short KMS integration guide. we can do SAML SSO or provide short-lived service accounts for the POC.
00:02:23 Dr. Priya Kapoor: timelinewise we need the mid-point review in ~3 weeks and an exec readout in early November. is that feasible?
00:02:30 Samira Ahmed: feasible if access is provisioned quickly. typical schedule: kickoff week 1, access and data week 2, run baseline benchmarks week 2 end, tuning week 3, mid-point review week 4, final tuning + exec readout week 6.
00:02:45 Michael Chen: dependencies: we must get VPC peering or a safe path for data, plus KMS keys. how long does that usually take?
00:02:54 Eli Torres: provisioning VPC peering and IAM often takes a few days on the customer side; if you have a network team we can give a checklist today. KMS integration depends on whether you want Redwood to call your KMS or use customer-managed keys in a private deployment; we have both options.
00:03:12 Laura Perez: prefer customer-managed KMS if we go private; for the pilot we might permit Redwood-hosted keys with strict retention if necessary.
00:03:19 Jordan Reed: that's a standard approach. we'll note both options in the SOW.
00:03:24 Nina Park: about cost modeling — can you run an apples-to-apples expected cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated/quantized?
00:03:33 Samira Ahmed: yes we'll estimate cost using your traffic profile and our quantization profiles. we'll include conservative and optimistic numbers.
00:03:42 Aaron Holt: on evaluation criteria for quality — we want a small eval set with clinical-style prompts and human raters for correctness and hallucination rate.
00:03:50 Dr. Priya Kapoor: yes, quality is non-negotiable. throughput and latency are in service of clinician UX.
00:03:58 Jordan Reed: good. demo/bench plan: Samira will prepare benchmark scripts and a repo with instructions; Jordan will send SOW and security artifacts; Veridian to provision access and dataset.
00:04:10 Michael Chen: any blockers we foresee? region constraints - we need EU data residency for a subset of patients, and also FIPS/HSM requirements for some keys.
00:04:20 Eli Torres: we can route EU traffic to EU-backed hosts and use customer-managed HSM for keys in private deployment, but that'll add setup time. we'll flag the mid-point review to discuss Dedicated if latency is not met.
00:04:33 Nina Park: ok. propose kickoff 2025-10-09; can Jordan send calendar invite?
00:04:39 Jordan Reed: yes I'll send today.
00:04:42 Samira Ahmed: I'll share the benchmark plan by 2025-10-08 and a config checklist for the networking and KMS steps.
00:04:50 Laura Perez: I'll confirm internal stakeholders and get our security pack to you by 2025-10-07.
00:04:55 Jordan Reed: great. any other questions?
00:05:00 Michael Chen: one small thing — do you have a preferred testing harness? we use JMeter and locust internally.
00:05:07 Samira Ahmed: we provide a lightweight locust harness but can export results to whatever tool you prefer; we'll publish a CSV and Grafana dashboard snapshots.
00:05:16 Dr. Priya Kapoor: sounds good.
00:05:18 Jordan Reed: ok we'll recap next steps in the follow-up email. thanks everyone.
00:05:22 Meeting end notes: follow ups to include SOW, SOC2 docs, benchmark scripts link, calendar invites. Formal mid-point review scheduled for 2025-10-24. Exec readout tentatively 2025-11-05.
